units.title: Last-digit rules: 2, 5 and 10
units.description: Decide divisibility by 2, 5 and 10 from the last digit alone.
learningObjectives: State the last-digit tests for 2, 5 and 10
Explain why the last digit is enough

blocks.text: Every place except the units place is a multiple of 10, and 10 is divisible by 2, 5 and 10. So the leading part of any number always passes these tests, and only the last digit can spoil it.
Divisibility by 2, 5 or 10 is decided entirely by the units digit.

content.text: 341 ends in 1: divisible by neither 2, 5 nor 10. 250 ends in 0: divisible by 2, 5 **and** 10. 975 ends in 5: divisible by 5 only.
Notice that any number divisible by 10 is automatically divisible by both 2 and 5 — because 10 = 2 × 5.

blocks.question: Which single last digit makes a number divisible by 2, 5 and 10 at once?

options.text: No single digit can do this

blocks.explanation: Only numbers ending in 0 are divisible by 10 — and they are automatically divisible by 2 and 5 as well.

units.title: Divisibility by 4 and 8
units.description: Use the last two or three digits to test divisibility by 4 and 8.
learningObjectives: Test divisibility by 4 using the last two digits
Test divisibility by 8 using the last three digits

blocks.text: 100 is divisible by 4 (100 = 4 × 25). So chopping a number into its last two digits and the rest, the 'rest' part is always divisible by 4 — only the last two digits matter.
The same logic climbs a place: 1,000 is divisible by 8 (1,000 = 8 × 125), so divisibility by 8 depends only on the last **three** digits.
By 4: check the last two digits. By 8: check the last three digits.

content.text: For 53,216: last two digits are 16, and 16 = 4 × 4, so 53,216 is divisible by 4. Last three digits are 216, and 216 = 8 × 27, so it is divisible by 8 too.
For 91,530: last two digits are 30, and 30 is not a multiple of 4 — so 91,530 fails the test for 4, and therefore for 8 as well (every multiple of 8 is a multiple of 4).

blocks.title: Shortcut inside the shortcut
blocks.text: To check whether the last three digits are divisible by 8, halve them twice. If both halvings give whole numbers, the original is divisible by 8: 216 → 108 → 54, all whole, so 216 passes.

blocks.question: Is 12,744 divisible by 8?

options.text: No, because 44 is not divisible by 8
It cannot be decided without full division

blocks.explanation: Only the last three digits matter for 8: 744 = 8 × 93, so the whole number is divisible by 8. Note that divisible by 4 does not imply divisible by 8.

units.title: Divisibility by 6
units.description: Test divisibility by 6 by combining the tests for 2 and 3.
learningObjectives: Combine the tests for 2 and 3 to test divisibility by 6
Explain why both conditions are needed

blocks.text: Since 6 = 2 × 3, a number is divisible by 6 exactly when it is divisible by **both** 2 and 3. Both conditions are needed — 9 passes the test for 3 but fails for 2, and 4 passes for 2 but fails for 3; neither is divisible by 6.
For a divisor written as a product of coprime parts (6 = 2 × 3), the number must pass every part's test.

content.text: Step 1 — even? Last digit 6 is even ✓

blocks.question: Which of these numbers is divisible by 6?
blocks.explanation: 5,118 is even and its digit sum 5+1+1+8 = 15 is divisible by 3. The others fail one test each: 5,119 is odd, 5,120 has digit sum 8, 5,123 is odd with digit sum 11.

units.title: Combining the rules
units.description: Test composite divisors like 12, 15 and 24 by chaining simple rules.
learningObjectives: Split a composite divisor into coprime factors
Chain rule tests to settle divisibility quickly

blocks.text: Any composite divisor splits into coprime parts, and the number must pass **all** parts. Choosing coprime parts matters: 12 = 4 × 3 works (4 and 3 share no factor), but 12 = 2 × 6 does not — 18 is divisible by both 2 and 6 yet not by 12.

rows: Digit sum by 3, last two digits by 4
Digit sum by 3, last digit 0 or 5
Digit sum by 3, last three digits by 8
Last digit even, digit sum by 9
blocks.caption: Chaining tests for composite divisors

blocks.text: A number is divisible by a composite divisor iff it passes the tests of every coprime factor in the split.

content.text: Test by 3: digit sum 6 + 1 + 3 + 2 = 12, divisible by 3 ✓

blocks.question: Is 2,475 divisible by 15?

options.text: Yes — digit sum 18 passes for 3 and it ends in 5
No — it fails the test for 3
No — it fails the test for 5
It cannot be decided without dividing

blocks.explanation: 2,475 = 15 × 165. It ends in 5 (passes for 5) and its digit sum 2+4+7+5 = 18 passes for 3, so it passes for 15.
